Question:
Do those who took course X report different comfort levels than those who did not take the course?
(this is question 3)

Cleaning Data
```{r}
library(tidyverse)

bg_clean <- read_csv("C:/Users/csola/OneDrive/Desktop/Pstat 197 (Capstone)/Class Survey/module0-class-survey/data/background-clean.csv")

# separate_rows() function worked better than pivot_longer()
# here, sep = ", " separates by every comma and space
bg_clean_long <- separate_rows(bg_clean, courses, sep = ", ")

bg_clean_long_info <- select(bg_clean_long, response_id, courses, prog.comf, math.comf, stat.comf)
#bg_clean_long_info

#head(bg_clean_long, 25)
```



Plot of number of students who took each course:
(similar to Tidyverse basics section material)
[This was to just have it here for reference]
```{r}
course_count <- count(bg_clean_long, courses, name = "n")

ggplot(data = course_count, aes(x = n, y = reorder(courses, n))) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 50, by = 2)) +
  labs(x = "Number of people who took the course")
```



Dot Plot of mean(prog, math, stats):
```{r}
#library(ggplot2)

course_means <- bg_clean_long %>%
  group_by(courses) %>% # need to group by courses to get the mean comfort for each course
  summarise(
    mean_prog = mean(prog.comf),
    mean_math = mean(math.comf),
    mean_stat = mean(stat.comf),
    count = n() # this is counting the number of responses for each course but plot doesn't need
    )
#course_means

# pivot_longer moves column names to and means to rows, and name the new column names
plot_data <- course_means %>%
  pivot_longer( 
    cols = c(mean_prog, mean_math, mean_stat),
    names_to = "subject",
    values_to = "mean_comf"
    )
# plot_data

ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = mean_comf, y = courses, color = subject)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, position = position_dodge(width = 0.7)) +
  labs(x = "Mean comfort", y = NULL, color = "Subject") 
# position = ... green is slightly lower, red is also slightly lower, and blue is slightly higher in their positions to avoid complete overlapping.
```
